clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old man with diabetes presented with acute bilateral vision loss (right eye: complete, 0/10; left eye: partial, 5/10) and moderate headache 4 days after discharge from hospitalization for COVID-19 (confirmed by PCR 3 weeks prior). On admission, he was afebrile with right pupil nonreactive and left pupil reactive; fundoscopy was normal bilaterally. Brain MRI showed diffuse restricted bilateral foci in parietal and occipital lobes on DWI, suggesting acute infarction. Lumbar puncture revealed negative results for HSV-1/2, VZV IgM, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR, ruling out common viral encephalitis. Laboratory tests showed normal CBC, biochemistry, and negative vasculitis, anti-MOG, anti-NMDA receptor antibodies, and current SARS-CoV-2 PCR. The patient deteriorated with confusion and right hemiparesis, prompting treatment with methylprednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/day for 3 days), followed by prednisolone maintenance (1 mg/kg/day), and subsequently IVIg (25 g/day for 5 days), which resulted in improvement of mental state and clinical symptoms. At 3-month follow-up, the patient remained blind (no light perception) without pupillary light reflex, but muscle strength returned to normal with persistent wide-based gait; MRI showed no new lesions. The patient was maintained on prednisolone (10 mg/day) and warfarin (INR 2.2).

final.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old man with diabetes presented with acute bilateral vision loss (right eye: complete, 0/10; left eye: partial, 5/10) and moderate headache 4 days after discharge from hospitalization for COVID-19 (confirmed by PCR 3 weeks prior). On admission, he was afebrile with right pupil nonreactive and left pupil reactive; fundoscopy was normal bilaterally. Brain MRI showed diffuse restricted bilateral foci in parietal and occipital lobes on DWI, suggesting acute infarction. Lumbar puncture revealed negative results for HSV-1/2, VZV IgM, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR, ruling out common viral encephalitis. Laboratory tests showed normal CBC, biochemistry, and negative vasculitis, anti-MOG, anti-NMDA receptor antibodies, and current SARS-CoV-2 PCR. The patient deteriorated with confusion and right hemiparesis, prompting treatment with methylprednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/day for 3 days), followed by prednisolone maintenance (1 mg/kg/day), and subsequently IVIg (25 g/day for 5 days), which resulted in improvement of mental state and clinical symptoms. At 3-month follow-up, the patient remained blind (no light perception) without pupillary light reflex, but muscle strength returned to normal with persistent wide-based gait; MRI showed no new lesions. The patient was maintained on prednisolone (10 mg/day) and warfarin (INR 2.2).
